Package neqsim.process.mechanicaldesign.valve.choke

Class ChokeFlowCoefficient

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.mechanicaldesign.valve.choke.ChokeFlowCoefficient
public final class ChokeFlowCoefficient extends Object
Conversions between a choke flow coefficient (Cv), an equivalent orifice and a discharge coefficient.

The US flow coefficient is defined by water at 1000 kg/m3: a valve with Cv = 1 passes one US gallon per minute with a pressure drop of one psi. If all of that pressure drop is spent accelerating the fluid through the flow area (no pressure recovery, Bernoulli), the area that passes the Cv = 1 flow is 

 A1 = Q1 / sqrt(2 dP1 / rho_w) = 1.699e-5 m2   (an orifice of about 4.65 mm diameter)

For a real orifice with discharge coefficient Cd the geometric area is A = Cv A1 / Cd, which is equivalent to Cv = 46 224 Cd D^2 for the diameter D in metres. The discharge coefficient is the product of the contraction (vena contracta) and the energy-loss effects, depends on trim geometry and opening, and must be chosen for the valve in question. Converting Cv to a diameter manually, with the discharge coefficient that the downstream flow model will use, keeps the capacity of the flow model equal to the Cv of the data sheet.

The helper also converts measured flow and pressure drop into an observed Cv, which is the basis of choke condition monitoring (ChokeConditionMonitor).

    • observedCv

      public static double observedCv(double volumeFlowM3PerS, double densityKgPerM3, double pressureDropPa)
      Observed flow coefficient from a measured volume flow and pressure drop, treating the fluid as incompressible at the given density: Cv = Q_gpm sqrt(SG / dP_psi).

      For a gas or a flashing multiphase stream the value is an equivalent coefficient on the upstream mixture density, adequate for comparing an observation with a theoretical curve of the same definition but not as a sizing result.

      Parameters:
      volumeFlowM3PerS - volume flow at upstream conditions [m3/s], positive
      densityKgPerM3 - upstream fluid density [kg/m3], positive
      pressureDropPa - pressure drop across the choke [Pa], positive
      Returns:
      observed Cv [US Cv]
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if an input is not positive and finite
